In [[combinatorics|combinatorial]] mathematics, '''Toida's conjecture''', due to [[Shunichi Toida]] in 1977,<ref>S. Toida: "A note on Adam's conjecture", Journal of Combinatorial Theory (B), pp. 239–246, October–December 1977</ref> is a refinement of the disproven [[Ádám's conjecture]] from 1967.

==Statement==
Both [[conjecture]]s concern [[circulant graph]]s. These are graphs defined from a positive [[integer]] <math>n</math> and a set <math>S</math> of positive integers.
Their vertices can be identified with the numbers from 0 to <math>n-1</math>, and two vertices <math>i</math> and <math>j</math> are connected by an edge
whenever their difference [[modular arithmetic|modulo]] <math>n</math> belongs to set <math>S</math>. Every [[group automorphism|symmetry]] of the [[cyclic group]] of addition modulo <math>n</math>
gives rise to a [[graph automorphism|symmetry]] of the <math>n</math>-vertex circulant graphs, and Ádám conjectured (incorrectly) that these are the only symmetries of the circulant graphs.

However, the known [[counterexample]]s to Ádám's conjecture involve sets <math>S</math> in which some elements share non-trivial [[divisor]]s with <math>n</math>.
Toida's conjecture states that, when every member of <math>S</math> is [[relatively prime]] to <math>n</math>, then the only symmetries of the circulant graph for <math>n</math> and <math>S</math> are symmetries coming from the underlying cyclic group.

==Proofs==

The conjecture was proven in the special case where ''n'' is a [[prime power]] by Klin and Poschel in 1978,<ref>Klin, M.H. and R. Poschel: The Konig problem, the isomorphism problem for cyclic graphs and the method of Schur rings, Algebraic methods in graph theory, Vol. I, II., Szeged, 1978, pp. 405–434.</ref> and by Golfand, Najmark, and Poschel in 1984.<ref>Golfand, J.J., N.L. Najmark and R. Poschel: The structure of S-rings over Z2m, preprint (1984).</ref>

The conjecture was then fully proven by Muzychuk, Klin, and Poschel in 2001 by using [[Schur algebra]],<ref>Klin, M.H., M. Muzychuk and R. Poschel: The isomorphism problem for circulant graphs via Schur ring theory, Codes and Association Schemes, American Math. Society, 2001.</ref> and simultaneously by Dobson and [[Joy Morris|Morris]] in 2002 by using the [[classification of finite simple groups]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Dobson | first1 = Edward
 | last2 = Morris | first2 = Joy | author2-link = Joy Morris
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Electronic Journal of Combinatorics
